### Summary

The numerics switches and the YAML options can be combined, but not every combination has a test. The table in this
section says, for each combination a registered test exercises, which test it is and what it asserts, so a reader
can tell a combination that is checked from one that merely runs.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Maps switch combinations to registered assertions.

**Data.** CTest registrations and child-process arms in; coverage rows out.

**Placement.** Match the registration to the arm before interpreting a result.

**Activation.** Choose an explicit row and sanitize inherited switch values.

**Guarantee / limits.** A setup guard is not an accuracy test; registration is not execution.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-matrix-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

Table key: XC is `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`; the other selectors are deck keys under `dynamics:` (CO is
`conversion-order`, FC `flux-covariance`, MC `x1-mass-covariance`). The corrected face work has no selector
(@sec-ch12-radial-exact). `<b>` is the lower-case build suffix; "child" means a fresh process per arm, "CTest"
means the registration sets the value, and "test" means the test sets it on its own blocks.

### Derivation

Coverage is a relation between a configuration and a test assertion, not a probability or an accuracy
estimate. A row is supported only when both the registration and the test's actual arm agree; a guard
assertion supports setup behaviour, not an error norm. Check line `[C11]` states the relation as a table:
support is the conjunction of registration and arm over its four combinations, and of the four (assertion
kind, claim kind) pairs exactly one is unsupported, a guard assertion offered for an error norm
[check `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

First select a build that contains the required entries, then establish the import provenance, sanitize the
numerics switches, and launch the named arm. Compare the invariant that the gravity-work mode selects: energy
plus corrected potential energy on a grid with an $x_1$ measure, energy plus plain potential energy otherwise. Record
CPU or CUDA and the rank count with every measured result. The dependency figure draws an implication from XC to the fourth-order reference and a switch for the corrected
work; the code at the pin has neither. The table above is the authority.

### Code

**How to use it.** Pick one row, inspect its registration, then execute its exact test name in a compatible
build. For the CO 4 seam row in a Release build:

```bash
env -u SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT \
  ctest --test-dir build -R '^test_x1_seam_split_co4_face_density.release$' --output-on-failure
```

`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` is removed with `-u`, not set to `0`: the arm asserts that the variable is unset. The test
sets `conversion-order` 4 on its own columns, so no extra YAML is needed. A missing entry, disabled arm or empty
selection is not evidence. Setup refusals constrain configuration only, and cannot certify an error norm.

The `seam_arm` registration in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}} selects the environment and assertion:

```cmake
seam_arm(_co4_face_density "" co4_face_density_at_the_seam_split_matches_one_block)
```

The first argument supplies the name suffix, the second the environment (empty here), and the third the gtest
case. The coverage relation of `[C11]` requires both this registration and the executed arm to match the claim.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| seam arms | {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}} | `seam_arm` | XC, CO, MC |
| python entries | {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}} | `snapy_add_python_test` | FC, MC, `SNAP_ANOMALY` |
| cuda entries | {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}} | `SKIP_RETURN_CODE` | `CUDA` |
| mc guard | {{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.x1_mass_covariance_needs_3_x1_cells >}} | `x1_mass_covariance_needs_3_x1_cells` | MC |
| co arms | {{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.co4_face_density_at_the_seam_split_matches_one_block >}} | `g_conv_order` | CO |
| xc arms | {{< code tests/test_x1_centroid_rest.py run >}} | `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` | XC |
| fc arms | {{< code tests/test_horizontal_flux_covariance.py ARMS >}} | `ARMS` | FC |

| fc seams arms | {{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py main >}} | `DIFF_TOL` | FC |

1. Read the CTest registrations and their environments. The anchor `seam_arm` is in

2. Read the arms each script creates, in one process or in child processes. The anchor `ARMS` of the

3. Enter a row only where the registration and the arm agree.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| all entries in the matrix | registered assertions only | see the individual scheme tables | no runtime results in this chapter |
| `configuration_check.py` `[C11]` (report check) | the registration/arm support relation | exact symbolic or Boolean equality | the independent check |

: Source assertions, not new solver measurements. {#tbl-ch12-matrix-tests}

No snapy runtime test is executed for this chapter. CUDA and multi-rank entries describe registration only.
The independent checks and their outputs are catalogued in @sec-ch16-ch12-tests.

The independent report check verifies the registration/arm support relation in `[C11]`.[^ch12-matrix-run]
It models the stated contract; it does not execute the compiled solver.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Numerical MC behaviour, XC together with FC, XC on gnomonic grids, FC across MPI ranks, and the wider simultaneous
combinations have no registered evidence. CO 4 has fitted-order tests (`test_conversion_order_python`), whose
thresholds were not re-read line by line for this edit. An all-keys combination is not covered.

The complete switch inventory is this section.
:::
